parsed.explanation: Uncommonly enforced sodomy law (up to 1 year) is secondary, but documented arrests for sexuality/gender identity and deterrence from reporting show it operates as a police lever. Concealment is the norm, private spaces only, anti-LGBTQ sentiment and a 2024 harsh bill remain active threats, and no trans-specific visitor protection, facility, border or violence-recourse practice is documented. No execution, torture, universal registration, or documented trans-specific offence; employment protection is resident-facing only. Combined regime leaves an outed visitor with imprisonment, outing and no effective recourse risk, above organised-targeting tiers but below 0.45.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Some LGBTQ people arrested on basis of sexuality or gender identity; sodomy offence carries up to 1 year imprisonment, enforcement uncommon.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Attackers using LGBTQ status can lead to arrest; criminal law deters victims reporting to police.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming hormone therapy and surgery not available domestically, so visitor cannot obtain transition-related care.
care_services.interaction: Absence is documented at time of coverage; later availability unresolved. No medication seizure documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Criminalises consensual same-sex conduct, no same-sex marriage; president defended laws; fliers targeted supporters in 2012; Oct 2024 legislator seeking support for harsh anti-homosexuality bill.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Section 2.4(b)(iii) 2015 labour statute bars employment discrimination by sex, gender identity or sexual orientation, resident-facing climate signal only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Employment protection coexists with criminalisation; its practical enforcement is unresolved and does not offset criminal exposure for a visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Related proposals would imprison children as young as 10 for gay sex; only at support-seeking stage Oct 2024, enacted status unresolved and not counted as law.
minors_guardians.interaction: Uncertainty for travelling minors/families, but no documented enacted minor-specific traveller rule.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Public concealment is documented norm; LGBTQ residents often hide identities, private spaces only. No trans-specific violence rate with denominator documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Existence of criminal law deters reporting; attackers using LGBTQ status documented as trigger for arrest, not protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented trans-visitor remedy, border, facility, custody or hate-crime recourse; 2013 MSM HIV figure is old and not trans-specific, given no weight.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin dossier extrapolated from criminalisation, active hostile legislation, concealment norm and no relief record; absence is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar thin recourse and birth-sex/unremedied risk language, but here no documented routine raids, extortion, or birth-sex prison placement and max term is 1 year, so higher than 0.25 organised custody pattern.

Similar deterrence and ineffective complaints after police stops/extortion, but here enforcement is described as uncommon rather than routine detention/fines for visitors, and no universal identity checks are documented; close to 0.35, slightly below or at it given concealment norm.

Higher than 0.45 because 0.45 harms are mainly exclusion/delay with imprisonment unlikely; here documented arrests for gender identity and a criminal imprisonment exposure plus no documented remedy make consequences more severe.
Much lower than 0.65: no national equality protection operating for visitors, no apology/compensation or reliable release documented, whereas 0.65 has working courts and advocacy intervention.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: a latent but usable criminal statute, documented gender-identity arrests, a concealment-norm society, active harsher legislation, unavailable transition care, and no documented visitor-facing protections or remedies interact to make outing consequential. The 2015 employment clause cannot offset this for a non-resident visitor under rubric 1, and the 2024 children's proposal remains uncertain, not enacted. No universal-exposure or lethal state practice is documented, keeping score above 0.25; documented imprisonment exposure and no recourse keep it below 0.45.
